races.name: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dreamasar
runners_data.note: Strong form profile — won twice at 10f on soft and standard, but this 12f on good to firm is a slight step up in trip; Billy Loughnane rides and Ed Walker's yard is in solid current form; positioned prominently, which suits this race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides this consistent five-year-old, but a hold-up style on a likely-steady tempo is a tactical disadvantage today; five recent runs all on good ground show he handles conditions, though his best form has come over 8f rather than 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Moody
runners_data.note: Two wins from two runs at 12f on good and heavy suggest the trip is right, and this is a lightly-raced four-year-old with upside; however, 74 days off the track is worth noting, and while he wants to race prominently, the crowded prominent pack may force him to cover more ground than ideal. The headgear note (tongue-tie) adds an unknown variable on return.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on this consistent mare, who has run exclusively at 11-12f and placed on good ground repeatedly; her record of 1W3P in six similar-going runs shows she rarely wins but rarely runs badly either, making her a reliable prominent type who fits the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: One Look
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-maker here, rated 111 and the highest OR in the field; James Doyle partners, and trainer Twomey has two runners today; a headgear note (hood) and a record of 2W7P in similar going underlines his staying power, though his [STYLE_FIT] tag acknowledges he may be pushed beyond his ideal front-running comfort zone if rivals press.

runners_data.name: Rhapsody
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore pilots this four-year-old who has winning form over 9f on good ground, but her best trips have been 8-9f and this 1m2f on good to firm stretches her profile; she naturally wants to race prominently but is squeezed into a midfield slot by the competitive pace map, meaning Moore will need to be creative to find her optimal position.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer at heart, though the redistribution map places her in midfield; Robson De Aguiar's yard has not fired a winner from 14 runners in 14 days, and her recent form figures of 50-584 do not inspire confidence; 15th at 12f on good last time is a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this one-time winner over 10f on soft, but six outings show a horse who struggles to replicate that winning form on good ground; held up by style, which is the wrong end of a potentially modest tempo, and 41 days between runs adds a fitness question.

races.paceDynamic: One Look is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival prepared to push for the early lead, is set to control matters from the front at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at the Curragh. Dreamasar and Nyra are the most likely to sit prominently in behind, whilst Francophone and Subsonic will be held up and depend on a strong enough gallop to bring them into play late. The field contains more prominent-leaning types than the race shape can absorb — Moody, Rhapsody, and Spicy Margarita are all redistributed into midfield on the map, but realistically Moody and Rhapsody are the most likely to press forward and occupy those positions, squeezing Spicy Margarita toward the rear. A controlled, single-pace gallop dictated by One Look — unlikely to be seriously pressured — sets this race up most favourably for horses travelling prominently in the first three or four, who can quicken off a steady tempo rather than hold-up horses waiting for a strong pace that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: One Look Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If One Look leads without pressure and controls a moderate tempo throughout the 1m2f.
scenarios.body: One Look sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and kicks entering the straight, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to close the gap on fast ground; prominent horses who travel close to the pace are best placed to respond to any quickening. Dreamasar and Nyra, racing prominently, are the chief beneficiaries, along with One Look itself if it has enough in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Moody and Rhapsody push forward to join One Look and the race unfolds at a stronger, more contested clip.
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop develops between the prominent types, stretching the field entering the straight and ensuring a true test of quality at this distance; horses with proven form at 1m2f on good ground and tactical speed are rewarded. Moody, who has won twice at this trip, and Nyra, consistent at the distance, are the profiles that benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply enough in the straight to expose horses that have raced prominently, leaving a gap for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Francophone or Subsonic, held up and saving energy through the early stages, pounce if front-runners tire on a demanding Good to Firm surface in the final two furlongs; this scenario requires a strong gallop to have been set — possible but not the most likely shape given One Look's uncontested lead. Both closers need genuine pace to hunt down, and the race shape may simply not generate enough of it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments tactically, with multiple horses pulling wide or failing to settle, creating chaos in the pack.
scenarios.body: An unexpected mid-race injection of pace or a prominent rival going too soon allows a horse like Rhapsody or Spicy Margarita — both racing out of their natural role — to find daylight and outrun their redistribution disadvantage; this is a low-probability shape requiring multiple factors to misfire simultaneously. Rhapsody has winning form on good ground and is the more credible of the two in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: One Look's ability to control the tempo entirely unchallenged is the central tactical key — if Moody or Rhapsody push James Doyle's mount harder than expected in the first half-mile, the complexion of the race changes entirely.

Moody returns after 74 days off the track and will want to race prominently into a congested space; watch for interference or a bumpy early passage if Rhapsody also tries to press forward, as both are genuine prominent types competing for the same slots.

Francophone and Subsonic are both held up and depend on a pace that may never develop — if One Look is allowed to saunter in front, both closers could find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight on fast ground.

The Good to Firm going is confirmed for this race — Spicy Margarita's trainer has zero winners from 14 runners in the last 14 days, which is a meaningful form flag worth monitoring against her already-modest recent figures.

races.name: Liverpool FC Foundation Scurry Handicap

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner — Edward Lynam has won with her here at 5f on good and she steps up to 6½f today, which is the key query; if the extra furlong is within range she is a major player, sitting on a career high mark of OR 102 and partnered by W J Lee who rides her sympathetically.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: A two-time winner at 5f on good ground, Colin Keane takes the ride for J A Stack who is 2/6 in the last 14 days; suited by good-to-firm conditions and has the prominent style to track Keke directly, making him one of the most positionally-advantaged horses in the race.

runners_data.name: Tango Flare
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who relishes good ground — 14 of his last 15 runs have come on going in the good to firm range and he has two wins at 6f on it; needs the pace to be generous but his recent 1-2 form at this trip is a significant flag.

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator wearing a visor, eight years old but remains competitive at OR 99; sim-going record of 10 from 15 on good is respectable, though his recent finishing positions suggest he needs a strong pace to find his best — that may not materialise here.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: Prominent style but his best form has come on soft/good-to-soft ground — only 7 of his last 15 runs on similar going have been competitive and his one recent win came on soft; the good-to-firm conditions here are a genuine concern and he may be outpaced early.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Four wins from 10 starts at 6f on good ground including two in recent form — this horse has a strong profile for the conditions and John & Sean Quinn have had no trainers' runners in the last 14 days, suggesting Dark Thirty is a focused entry; prominent style suits the likely race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: City House
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form includes a string of placed efforts at 7f and 8f — dropping back to 6½f is a shortening of trip and headgear (tongue-tie) is worn; Adrian McGuinness has three runners in the race which suggests stable confidence is spread, and this may not be the stable's first string.

runners_data.name: Headmaster
runners_data.note: Trained by Edward Lynam alongside Keke — a yard with two runners and T14 of 1/4 — and his last two runs include a 6f win and a 7f second on good ground; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride and good-to-firm conditions tick a box given his Curragh form.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Recent form shows three wins and a string of thirds — consistent but not a winner on pure good ground, with just 3 from 15 on similar conditions historically; wears no headgear and is stepping up marginally in class, making him a reliable but not headline selection.

runners_data.name: Sir Les Patterson
runners_data.note: A claimer aboard (Jack Kearney, 3lb) and OR 92 after a string of mid-pack finishes on good — wears a hood (hg:p) and has course experience; recent form shows no win on good-to-firm going specifically and the low trainer strike rate over 14 days is a mild negative.

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent-going horse — in a field with this many pace types, he is likely to find himself racing wider or further back than ideal, which tempers his chance; his best form is over 5f on good going so the 6½f trip also represents an extension he may not fully see out.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: An authentic front-runner by inclination whose last win came at 7f on good — in this contest he cannot get his natural prominent berth given the volume of pace ahead of him, which means he races in an uncomfortable position; Wayne Lordan is a high-quality booking and this horse's course form at 6f-7f on good is not without merit.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins at 5-6f on good and a solid sim-going record of 12 from 15 — Wesley Joyce rides with a 3lb claim; needs the pace to set up a closing run and while the conditions suit, the 6½f trip extends his usual 5-6f comfort zone slightly.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who has raced 13 of his last 15 times on good going — conditions are familiar but finishing positions of 7, 9, 20 and another 7 in recent runs tell a story of a horse who is struggling to land a blow even when conditions suit; Chris Hayes cannot do much more than ride a clean race.

runners_data.name: Oro Blanco
runners_data.note: A hat-trick seeking three-year-old who has won two on the bounce at 6f and 7f on good going — his natural front-running style cannot be accommodated in this field and he will race off his preferred pitch; the going, trip and recent form are all positive but the tactical compromise is real and should temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has raced primarily over 5f on good and standard — stepping up to 6½f is the furthest he has been asked to go, and his sim-going record of 8 from 15 is moderate; headgear (hood) worn and the OR 81 mark is the lowest in the field, making this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature who in this race will be unable to hold his usual position — David Marnane sends him from Co. Tipperary and the visor headgear suggests he needs to be switched on; recent form includes a 6f win on standard and a second on good, but the trip is shorter than some recent outings and the positional squeeze is the main handicap here.

runners_data.name: Back Down Under
runners_data.note: Primarily a 5-6f performer who races prominently — his natural position will be compromised by the volume of pace horses in this field, and his sim-going record of 13 from 15 on good ground is strong even if his finishing positions in those runs are not always flattering; OR 79 is the second-lowest in the field.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie, trained by Adrian McGuinness who has three runners here — his best effort in recent form is a 2nd at 6f on good and he has course experience; the eight-year-old needs a strong tempo to find his late run and whether this race provides it is the critical variable.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has been redistributed to midfield on the map only because of field density — Denis Gerard Hogan has had three winners from 28 runners over 14 days, which is a solid strike rate; last ran just seven days ago and his recent 6f form includes a 2nd on good going, suggesting freshness is not an issue.

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Last ran 211 days ago — a significant absence that immediately flags freshness as the key question; a true prominent-type racer who could not hold that position in this field regardless, and the OR 80 mark after a 7-month break with no sim-going form from the current yard makes this a speculative entry at best.

races.paceDynamic: Keke is the confirmed front-runner here and, critically, faces no serious challenger for the lead — this is a single-pace-setter scenario on Good to Firm ground over 6½f at the Curragh, meaning a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a true searching test. With Keke dictating from the front unchallenged, the pace is unlikely to be suicidal, which historically favours horses who can sit just off the leader and pick up in the straight rather than deep closers making up ground from off the pace. The hold-up brigade — Tango Flare, The Highway Rat, Genesis, Moltophino, Go Athletico — will need the pace to stretch the field, but with a solo leader controlling tempo, late runners face a stiffer task. This field carries a significant volume of true prominent-racers — Oro Blanco, Red Evolution, Glory To Be, Gavoo, Back Down Under, and Leveraging — none of whom can all hold natural positions simultaneously, meaning scrimmaging early is probable and some of that energy will be wasted in the first two furlongs. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can sit prominently just behind Keke in a compact group and quicken on the good-to-firm surface are most favoured — the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile wins this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keke Controls, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Keke gets a clean lead, sets a sustainable tempo, and the race develops as a classic front-runner's gallop with chasers landing on its quarters at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Keke bowls along uncontested through the first half-mile on the good-to-firm Curragh surface, the field settling into a compact group behind, and the horses tracking the leader in second and third have first run into the straight with momentum; prominent types who secure a clean run from the good-to-firm draw benefit from a predictable, metronomic tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the volume of true prominent types fighting for position creates an overfast early pace that burns out the chasers and leaves a genuine late closer with ground to make up.
scenarios.body: The scrimmage for position among the many prominent-natured runners — Oro Blanco, Gavoo, Glory To Be and others — lifts the tempo beyond what Keke intended, stretching the field and leaving real ground-closers with a genuine target; on good-to-firm going the Curragh straight rewards a sustained gallop and a horse with a finishing kick that has been produced wider from a midfield position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Keke Outstays All, Front Runs Home
scenarios.trigger: If Keke's controlled front-running on good-to-firm ground proves impossible to reel in given the absence of a pressure horse and a weak late challenge from the field.
scenarios.body: Keke, trained by Edward Lynam who handles front-runners at the Curragh with precision, maintains a metronomic stride throughout and is simply never headed, with chasers failing to close on the firmer ground through the straight; this scenario unfolds if the hold-up types run into traffic and the prominent runners have done too much early, leaving Keke's advantage intact.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pac Unravels, Big Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution chaos is at its most extreme — every prominent type burns energy early, Keke is swamped, and a complete outsider finds a seam late at a monster price.
scenarios.body: A bunched, scrappy early contest sees multiple prominent-natured horses crowding one another, pace collapses in the middle of the race and then surges again, creating an uneven tempo that unsettles the market leaders; a hold-up or redistributed runner who finds clear daylight on the outside in the final furlong profits from the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Keke's stamina over 6½f is the race's pivotal question — if she ties up in the final furlong having led unchallenged, the chasers directly behind her (Dark Thirty, Bodhi Bear, Headmaster) are poised to pick up the pieces immediately.

The cluster of six redistributed prominent types — Oro Blanco, Red Evolution, Glory To Be, Gavoo, Back Down Under, Leveraging — will create a scrimmage in the first two furlongs; watch for a bump in pace around the 5f pole that could catch hold-up horses flat-footed.

races.name: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Bucanero Fuerte
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent-racer whose strongest form is at 5-6f on good ground (placed here in similar conditions), but this field's pace saturation means he is structurally pushed to midfield — his 56-day absence and Robson De Aguiar's quiet 14-day record (0/14) add further doubt.|

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with back-to-back Curragh 5f wins on good ground, trained by the in-form Crisford yard (6/21 T14), and well-suited to sitting just off a steady Jakajaro pace before producing a sustained challenge; has the course form and the profile to be the biggest threat.|

runners_data.name: Jakajaro
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, Robert Cowell's five-year-old has winning form at 5f on good ground and Jamie Spencer will use his natural role to dictate; maps slightly out of role in probability terms only because his 32-day break and a STYLE_FIT flag suggest he may be sharper when truly pressed.|

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer with four wins at the trip on good ground (14/15 sim-going), but displaced into a hold-up mapping by sheer weight of prominent types in this field — Chris Hayes will likely push for closer order and the horse's natural forcing style should emerge.|

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: Colin Keane gets on a horse with winning form at 5f on good ground for in-form Loughnane (4/14 T14), but like Bucanero Fuerte, the glut of pace-committed runners means he cannot race where he wants; his best form requires a prominent pitch he is unlikely to secure.|

runners_data.name: Rosy Affair
runners_data.note: George Boughey's five-year-old has excellent recent form (win and placed from last three) and Billy Loughnane is a key booking; she races on 132lbs versus the heavier loads of the older horses, and her 5f form on good ground positions her ideally to challenge from a genuine prominent berth.|

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's three-year-old is stepping back from 6f with modest recent form (0 from last 4, best run a second at 5f); mapped to midfield because the prominent spots are full, and his sim-going record here (7/10) is the weakest of the group — Wayne Lordan faces an uphill task.|

runners_data.name: Charles Darwin
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners a three-year-old with three wins at 5f on good ground and strong class credentials from the O'Brien yard, mapped to hold-up but naturally a pace-pressing type; if the race scenario collapses in front of him, he is the most dangerous of the displaced horses on ability.|

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's three-year-old showed a 5f win at Curragh on good ground and sits highest-rated alongside Jakajaro on OR=110; Gavin Ryan should be able to secure a genuine prominent position in this field, making her a live contender if she gets the tactical setup she needs.|

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: De Aguiar's second string carries 128lbs as a three-year-old and her recent form has been patchy (6th, 4th, 7th last three); displaced to midfield by the pace congestion and Dylan Browne McMonagle will need a fast-developing race to bring her into contention from outside her natural position.|

races.paceDynamic: Jakajaro is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jamie Spencer can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on the Good to Firm Curragh turf over five furlongs. The field is saturated with prominent-running types — Bucanero Fuerte, Partisan Hero, Brussels, and Ipanema Queen all want to race prominently but cannot all do so, meaning several will be shuffled back into unnatural midfield positions rather than exerting genuine pressure on Jakajaro's pace. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate; of those, Cover Up, Rosy Affair, and Havana Anna are most likely to actually secure their preferred position just off the pace. With Jakajaro able to control tempo unchallenged and a fast surface rewarding those who travel through the race rather than make up ground late, the race shape strongly favours horses that can sit second or third and sustain their effort — genuine prominent-to-pace-holding profiles win here, and those shuffled to midfield against their nature face a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jakajaro Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jakajaro is allowed to set a measured, uncontested pace from the front and Jamie Spencer engineers a solo lead throughout.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressurise him early, Jakajaro can dictate fractions on the Good to Firm ground and use his 5f sharpness to hold on; horses that want to sit just off the pace in second and third must produce a sustained run rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Cover Up or Rosy Affair track Jakajaro closely throughout and a smooth, well-timed challenge in the final furlong proves decisive.
scenarios.body: A genuinely prominent horse that travels into the race without expending energy fighting for position can absorb a controlled pace and assert; both Cover Up (back-to-back Curragh wins at 5f) and Rosy Affair (strong recent form) fit this profile exactly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If Jakajaro misses the break or the race somehow develops a stronger tempo than expected and horses from behind get a meaningful chance.
scenarios.body: Charles Darwin and Kendall Roy are mapped to hold-up positions but are genuinely prominent types displaced by the crowded pace contingent, so a true late run requires pace breakdown rather than natural closing ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Field Bunched
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse their mapped positions and surge for the early lead, creating a compressed, scrimmaging early pace.
scenarios.body: Should Bucanero Fuerte, Brussels, or Ipanema Queen ignore their redistributed positions and force their way into the early argument, the race becomes ragged and the final-furlong dash is thrown open; Charles Darwin's class gives him an edge if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Jakajaro's early strides are critical — if Jamie Spencer gets a clean break and establishes the lead unchallenged in the first two furlongs, a large portion of the field's tactical flexibility is immediately removed and the race becomes his to lose.

Cover Up and Rosy Affair will contest the same prominent position just off Jakajaro's heels — watch how James Doyle and Billy Loughnane react at the break, as whichever secures the cleaner rail or air position will be structurally advantaged for the run-in.

Havana Anna (OR=110, Gavin Ryan) is the highest-rated runner alongside Jakajaro and is capable of sitting prominent naturally — if she travels smoothly in second or third, she should not be underestimated regardless of her 3yo weight allowance.

Charles Darwin (Ryan Moore, OR=107) is a genuine prominent type pushed to the hold-up mapping — watch his position at the two-furlong marker; if Moore has managed to sit third or fourth rather than tailing off, his class makes him dangerous in a compressed finish.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the headline description reading Good — faster conditions favour horses with high cruising speeds and will compress finishing times, reducing the margin for error for any horse that gets shuffled back early.

races.name: GAIN Railway Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Won over five furlongs on Good ground and shaped with promise stepped up to six, but with Celeron and Switching Sides likely to claim the prime prominent slots off Tribeca's lead, Lordan may find this horse racing further back than ideal for an A P O'Brien runner that wants to be travelling handy.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Beaten only 15 lengths on debut then bolted up over this exact course, distance and going — the profile of a horse who improved sharply once encountering six furlongs, and with Oisin Murphy aboard, expect him to slot in as the principal pressing rival to Tribeca; his OR=120 is matched only by Switching Sides and he merits respect.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount won over six furlongs on Good ground but has been placed and beaten already at this level; the bigger issue is that, with so many prominent types in this field, Moore may find himself further back than the horse's form requires, diluting the chance of the horse who ideally wants to be rolling through mid-race from a handy pitch.

runners_data.name: Immortal Guard
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts over six furlongs at the Curragh on Good ground and trained by De Aguiar alongside Tribeca, yet pushed back to a hold-up position on the map because of the field's prominent bias; his natural game is to be on the pace, so watch for Donagh O'Connor trying to push forward early — if he gets a prominent berth his form makes him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Switching Sides
runners_data.note: Won over six furlongs on Good ground at Listed level and ran a solid second in similar conditions — form that reads well for this surface and trip; Shane Foley is an astute claimer of position at the Curragh and, at OR=120, this filly has the class to track Tribeca and challenge strongly in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Dropped in OR to 90 but has won and placed over six furlongs on Good ground at the Curragh; the redistribution context means Joyce will struggle to get the forward berth this horse needs, and facing rivals rated 30 points higher makes a winner's position difficult, though a clean run could see him involved for minor honours.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, OR=120, with a convincing six-furlong win on Good ground at the Curragh for De Aguiar; Colin Keane will attempt to control tempo from the front and, if he gets away cleanly and rations the effort, the lack of a natural rival to press him is a significant tactical asset at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Tribeca is the confirmed front-runner and, in a field where every other runner is genuinely prominent-natured, she is likely to get a clean, uncontested lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground over six furlongs at the Curragh. The pace will be honest — Group 2 class on a fast surface demands it — but with no dedicated rival to press her through the early stages, Tribeca should control tempo and conserve energy for the final two furlongs. Celeron and Switching Sides, the two highest-rated rivals at OR=120, are natural prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader and pounce in the straight, making the real race a duel between the leader and those two closers-in-behind. This shape strongly favours horses who can race handily just off a lone front-runner and produce a clean, sustained finish — pure hold-up horses are disadvantaged on this flat, fast track. The field is overloaded with prominent types: Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator cannot all settle in their natural prominent berths, and Celeron and Switching Sides, with higher ratings and stronger recent form, are best placed to actually secure those prime positions just off Tribeca's lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tribeca Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tribeca leads uncontested and sets a true-but-not-suicidal pace, allowing Celeron or Switching Sides to track and pounce.
scenarios.body: Tribeca dictates from the front on a fast surface and the race develops into a sustained gallop that suits horses travelling smoothly in second or third; the premium prominent positions deliver a clear advantage in the home straight. Celeron and Switching Sides, both OR=120 with winning six-furlong form on Good ground, are ideally placed to deliver a decisive finish challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tribeca Wins Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Tribeca's uncontested lead proves too comfortable and no rival can find enough in the final furlong to reel her in.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to press Tribeca in the first two furlongs, she bowls along at a controlled gallop, rations her effort, and has reserves left to repel challengers; Good to Firm ground suits a horse with a clean action going forward. This is a genuine scenario given the sole front-runner status and the redistribution chaos among her rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble, Prominent Crowding
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types battle for position early, creating a faster-than-expected tempo that blows out the leaders.
scenarios.body: Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator all attempt to race in their natural prominent position and generate unexpected pressure on Tribeca, forcing a stronger gallop that leaves the field weakened entering the final furlong. A horse who manages to settle slightly off the pace through the early scramble, such as Switching Sides or Confucius, would benefit most from the resulting strong-pace finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario unfolds in a chaotic or unusually strong fashion and a lower-rated runner capitalises on positional chaos.
scenarios.body: The Scallionator has winning six-furlong form on Good ground and, if the redistribution of prominent runners creates a messy race where fancied horses are blocked or unbalanced, a horse at long odds with place form in similar conditions can steal a place or more. This is low-probability given class differentials but the congested prominent group makes it non-trivial.

watchPoints.text: Immortal Guard is mapped to hold-up but his three-from-three Curragh record over six furlongs suggests Donagh O'Connor will push forward — if he successfully forces his way prominent early, he becomes a serious danger whose form is superior to his current market position may suggest.

Monitor the draw and early positions of Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator — all three are natural prominent types who cannot all find their spot, and any jostling or checking in the first furlong could compromise multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

Tribeca's lead is only uncontested if Celeron and Switching Sides are content to sit second and third — if either jockey decides to go with her or go around her, the tempo spikes and the wire-to-wire scenario collapses quickly.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race — all seven runners have Good-ground form, but Celeron and Switching Sides both show their best figures specifically on Good going over six furlongs at this track, which is a meaningful edge on the day.

races.name: Juddmonte Irish Oaks (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for Aidan O'Brien and Ryan Moore with two wins in similar going, but her natural front-rank style means she will be jostling for position in a field overloaded with prominent types — competing outside her ideal role today.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this O'Brien hold-up filly who has six runs in Good ground without a win at the course level, a modest record in similar conditions that makes her a long shot if the pace doesn't quicken materially.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Won over this trip at the Curragh in Good and is a genuine prominent runner by inclination, though the sheer volume of pace rivals means Chris Hayes may find her shuffled back from her preferred position earlier than ideal.

runners_data.name: Composing
runners_data.note: Equipped with a hood and consistent in Good-ground races for O'Brien but without a win at this level; her naturally forward-going style is compromised by a deeply congested pace picture, and her recent form figures of 36-565 offer little encouragement at Group 1 level.

runners_data.name: Earth Shot
runners_data.note: William Haggas's charge arrives on the back of a Listed win and a solid second to a smart rival, has won twice in Good conditions over today's sort of trip, and as a genuine prominent-type (not redistributed) James Doyle can slot her ideally behind Thundering On.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f at the Curragh in Good and steps up to 1m4f with Oisin Murphy, who will be looking to sit second or third; trainer David Menuisier has a quiet 14-day record (0/8) but the horse's raw profile suits a pace-controlled Group 1 over this trip.

runners_data.name: Johanna Walsh
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this Joseph O'Brien filly who wears a tongue-tie and finished second in a 1m4f Listed in Good last time; her consistent form at this distance and the ability to track the pace naturally gives her a straightforward tactical route.

runners_data.name: Rebel Moon
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts, both on Good-to-Good/Firm ground, and a naturally prominent-going type — one of the most likely redistributed runners to actually push forward and race closer to Thundering On than the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Three from three for Jim Bolger, all in Good ground and progressively longer trips culminating in a 1m2f win at the Curragh — an aggressive front-runner by nature who is perhaps the likeliest of all the redistributed horses to push the pace alongside Thundering On today.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides this O'Brien hold-up type who showed wellbeing headgear and has a 1m4f win on soft; on Good to Firm today, 43 days since her last run, she needs both the pace to strengthen and the fast ground to suit her — two conditions that may not align.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner (OR 119) and the only confirmed front-runner in the field; Dylan Browne McMonagle can dictate from the front at a sustainable tempo on Good to Firm, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution that this Grade 1 trip over 1m4f in fast conditions is not yet a guaranteed comfort zone.

races.paceDynamic: Thundering On is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner Group 1 field and, with no genuine rival looking to dispute the lead, Dylan Browne McMonagle can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching early, which compresses the midfield and makes it harder for hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need from off the pace. Earth Shot, Inis Mor, and Johanna Walsh are the most credible prominent-position challengers who can legitimately track Thundering On and are not displaced by redistribution, giving them the clearest tactical route into the race. This shape strongly favours races-on-the-pace types and particularly those with a strong turn-of-foot at the business end — a controlled gallop into a late sprint rewards horses who are handily placed without having to fight for position. Note that the field contains considerably more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Amelia Earhart, Cameo, Composing, Rebel Moon, and Sparan Nua are all natural front-rank runners who are redistributed to midfield on the map — of these, Sparan Nua (unbeaten in three, aggressive handler) and Rebel Moon (two wins from two) are most likely to press forward and actually secure a prominent pitch ahead of the pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thundering On Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On leads uncontested at a steady-to-moderate gallop and the race becomes a tactical chess match that explodes in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Browne McMonagle settles Thundering On at a comfortable clip, saving plenty for the final quarter-mile on fast ground, and the race becomes a test of quality rather than stamina; prominently placed horses with a genuine change of gear are perfectly positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Spark Contest
scenarios.trigger: If Sparan Nua and/or Rebel Moon push forward aggressively alongside Thundering On, injecting genuine early pace and stretching the field.
scenarios.body: A quicker tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f will begin to test stamina reserves in the final furlong, and horses who combine a prominent position with proven staying power over the trip will be rewarded over those needing a late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns genuinely strong enough that the front rank ties itself up and a sweeping late challenge from deep proves viable.
scenarios.body: Beautify or Sugar Island, lobbing well off the pace in the early stages, would need a fast enough tempo to create the gap required — a scenario that relies on the front group burning each other out in a way the redistribution picture makes structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent runners create a congested, messy race where no single horse dominates and the winner comes from an unexpected quarter.
scenarios.body: A disorganised gallop with several horses out of their natural role fighting for ground mid-pack could produce a muddling, unrepresentative finish; horses with tactical versatility and a compact, efficient stride on fast ground benefit most in this chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Sparan Nua and Rebel Moon — both natural front-runners redistributed to midfield on the map — watch whether either pushes forward at the start to join Thundering On; if both do, the early pace transforms and the race shape shifts entirely.

Thundering On's solo lead could easily produce an artificially slow early gallop, compressing the field into a single-file sprint — watch for the pace figures in the opening half-mile to confirm whether this is a true test or a falsely-run affair.

Earth Shot is 30 days off her last run but arrives with two recent wins on Good ground at the right trip; watch for James Doyle positioning her immediately behind the leader from the outset, as any tactical error from a congested early break would compromise her chance.

Johanna Walsh wears a tongue-tie and has a habit of racing close to the pace; watch Colin Keane's positioning in the first furlong — if she gets a clean slot in second or third early, she becomes a significant beneficiary of the controlled Thundering On tempo.

The Good to Firm ground is faster than the official Good description in the race card — all going reports from the Curragh confirm Good to Firm for this race — which will shorten the overall time and slightly diminish the advantage of deep hold-up horses like Beautify and Sugar Island.

races.name: Hill Of Allen Stud Handicap

runners_data.name: Genchev
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong recent placed form at 10-12f on Good ground (three runs of 1W3P at similar going); Colin Keane's front-running craft will be central here, and dropping to the lead on a sound surface with just five rivals suits his style perfectly, though the STYLE_FIT tag as a P rather than pure L is noted.

runners_data.name: Vanir
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good at his last start and placed at 10f, so the trip and going are squarely in his favour; Ben Coen, in form for Murtagh's yard (2/22 T14), will likely sit just off Genchev and is the most natural beneficiary of a controlled pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Yousaynothingatall
runners_data.note: Three consecutive placings at 10-12f with a win at 10f on Soft suggests genuine ability, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top booking; however, his natural instinct to race prominently will be frustrated here because Genchev and Vanir own that ground, and his limited form on Good to Firm (0W1P from 2 sim-going runs) is a secondary concern.

runners_data.name: Noble Honour
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 10f on Good and consistent in form figures (2-32), making this trip and surface a reasonable match; like Yousaynothingatall, he is a horse who prefers to race with cover near the front but will find Genchev and Vanir unwilling to cede that territory, so Shane Foley must settle for a midfield berth — slightly against the grain of his profile.

runners_data.name: Trustmore
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U tag) and the weakest recent form in the field (7-56), with no wins or places from three runs on Good going; Oisin Murphy is a top jockey but even his presence cannot disguise that Trustmore lacks the form to threaten from his current mark of OR 73 with headgear applied.

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up runner and has placed twice at 10-12f on Good, so there is at least some course for optimism; she needs the pace to soften up the leaders from the back of a small field, which is a tall order when Genchev is likely to control the tempo without pressure.

races.paceDynamic: Genchev is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him hard for the lead, he should dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over the 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh. Vanir will press close behind from a prominent position, ensuring at least a competitive pace without it becoming a burning gallop, while Tanzanite Diamond will settle in rear as the only true hold-up type. The field contains more naturally prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate — Yousaynothingatall and Noble Honour are both genuine front-runners by inclination but are unlikely to get their natural positions with Genchev and Vanir already occupying that ground, meaning they will be forced to settle in a less comfortable midfield role. With a controlled, uncontested pace set by Genchev and Good to Firm ground rewarding horses that travel and quicken efficiently, this race shape strongly favours prominent or close-tracking profiles who can move through smoothly and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genchev Controls, Vanir Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Genchev sets a smooth, uncontested pace and the race is decided by a straight-line quickening duel between the front two.
scenarios.body: Genchev bowls along at a fair clip unchallenged, with Vanir sitting a length or two off the pace throughout; when the field enters the Curragh straight, Vanir's recent winning momentum and improving profile over this exact trip and going allow him to pick up and collar Genchev before the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Genchev's low weight and Colin Keane's front-running craft allow him to coast to the line without being overhauled.
scenarios.body: Genchev, having never truly been pressured, finds reserves in the final furlong that his rivals — forced to come from off a slow pace — cannot match; his course and distance form across 10-12f on Good ground makes this credible if the gallop is genuinely pedestrian.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace fragments the field and the race resolves into a flat-out slog in the final quarter mile, rewarding stamina over pure speed.
scenarios.body: Yousaynothingatall or Noble Honour, despite being pushed back from their natural front-running spots, keep tabs on the leaders near enough to benefit if the race becomes a grinding contest rather than a speed duel; their handicap marks are lower, offering a pounds-in-hand argument.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closer Gets In Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong early pace — perhaps triggered by Noble Honour or Yousaynothingatall pushing forward — burns off the leaders and opens the door for Tanzanite Diamond to come late.
scenarios.body: Tanzanite Diamond, the only genuine hold-up horse, would need the pace to collapse in front of her and a clear run from Adam Caffrey, both of which are unlikely given the field size and pace configuration; her improving 12f form on Good ground is the slim basis for inclusion.

watchPoints.text: Vanir is the primary danger to watch: if Ben Coen tracks Genchev closely throughout and produces a timely challenge turning for home, his recent 12f win on Good makes him a serious threat to control the race outcome.

Yousaynothingatall and Noble Honour will jostle for position in the early stages — watch for either jockey attempting to push forward past their designated midfield roles, which could briefly disrupt the pace picture in the first two furlongs.

Genchev's behaviour in the early stages is critical: if he is allowed to coast at a slow pace he becomes very difficult to peg back, but if Keane misjudges the tempo and goes too slow, the field bunches and his lead becomes worthless.

Trustmore carries the headgear flag and is an unknown quantity stylistically — if Oisin Murphy produces an unconventional ride or the unknown style resolves as a prominent one, he could briefly factor before his modest form figures reassert themselves.

races.name: WTW Willis Handicap

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner in the race; J P Murtagh runner ridden by 7lb claimer Jessica Maye, which is a watch point, but the horse has won at 5f on Good and shapes as the natural pace-setter — STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is rated a prominent type by the model, but in this 18-runner field she is effectively the lone leader.|

runners_data.name: Daneh Of Dandy
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride for Paul Twomey and this hold-up type has consistent 5f form in similar going; five of her last five are at this trip and she handles Good ground, though her best form is narrowly on softer surfaces — needs a strongly-run race to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Real Encounter
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Harrington-trained filly who has placed twice at 5f on Good ground and shapes as a natural settler just off the pace; her 6f runs suggest she stays well, which gives her an edge if the pace is moderate and the field kicks late.|

runners_data.name: Lamar Canyon
runners_data.note: Won last time at Slane over 5f on Standard and holds a genuine staying chance over the distance, but the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag is important — has the early pace to get a prominent spot but the handicapper may have caught up; 7lb claimer Adam Browne-Souza adds risk.|

runners_data.name: Final Melody
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount runs just six days after her last start and has been consistently placed at 5f on Standard, though this is only her second start on Good to Firm; trainer Lupini's runners have not fired recently (T14: 0/10) and that cold spell is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a 5f win at the Curragh on Good 14 days ago and Terry Casey's 7lb claim makes the weight very workable; a prominent racer who is proven fresh and at this track, he rates as one of the pace group's more interesting handicap contenders.|

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Gavin Ryan is always a positive booking in a 5f handicap at the Curragh; won at this trip on Good 15 days ago and showed solid 5f form at similar venues — hold-up style means he needs a clear run late but he is in career form right now.|

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: Seasoned six-year-old hold-up type who usually operates over 6-7f — dropping back to 5f is against his standard trip profile and the condensed field will make finding a run late difficult; Adrian McGuinness has had three runners in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Two wins and five places from fifteen runs on Good ground is an excellent strike rate; races prominently and handles 5f well for Willie McCreery, who is in decent form (T14: 2/18); headgear noted, though well exposed at this level now.|

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose true preference is to race well off the pace — in this crowded 18-runner sprint he will be pushed closer to the front than he wants, and his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that racing out of position compromises his chance; Colin Keane cannot manufacture pace that isn't there.|

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a prominent-style performer who was placed three times in fifteen Good-ground runs; comes off a fourth 14 days ago and is consistent if unspectacular — handles this trip and surface but needs to find improvement to get involved at the business end.|

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has won twice on Good ground at 5f, but the redistribution note tells the story — in an 18-runner 5f sprint she will inevitably be closer to the pace than her best form demands; headgear (blinkers) is a positive sharpener.|

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Andrew Oliver's three-year-old wore a tongue strap last time and has struggled for consistency (U-figure in recent form); best form is over shorter trips on Standard ground and the step up to this competitive handicap looks demanding on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Carrigans Grove
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides for the Patrick Flynn yard, which has had two winners from eleven in the last fortnight; a natural prominent racer, and given the crowded pace group, Hayes's experience makes him one of the likelier riders to actually hold that prominent slot — but recent form figures (8-4-0-0-7) are not encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Stable companion of Carrigans Grove and a genuine hold-up horse by style — has been well beaten in his last five runs and recent form over 6-7f doesn't inspire confidence at 5f on this surface; the redistribution to midfield doesn't change the reality that he is hard to back.|

runners_data.name: Nebrook Star
runners_data.note: 175 days since last run is the standout flag here — a three-year-old returning from a six-month layoff trained by Diego Dias, who has had just two runners in the fortnight; blinkers are noted as a headgear aid, and the horse has 5f form on Good, but this is a big ask on return.|

runners_data.name: Absoluteassignment
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes a true hold-up performer who has been well beaten in both recent Good-ground starts; best run was a second at 6f on Good, but 5f looks likely too sharp for this style and the 36-day gap between runs adds uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with blinkers and a tongue strap, holds a good record placing on Good ground (13/15 starts) but at the lowest OR in the field (60) needs everything to go right; a genuine rear-of-field type who will find the 5f trip stretching his late kick to its limit.|

races.paceDynamic: Namiid is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field at the Curragh over 5f on Good to Firm, and with no genuine rival to press her early she should be able to control the tempo from the outset and set a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a lung-bursting pace. Behind her, Real Encounter, Final Melody, Sovereign Cry, Happy Henry and Nouvel Espoir are all prominent types who will be scrapping for positions in the first two furlongs, creating moderate early pressure from outside the lead but unlikely to truly test Namiid's dominance. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Carrigans Grove is the most likely prominent runner to actually secure that position given course form, while Harry's Hill, Mary Shoelaces, Imperial Dream, Absoluteassignment and Tawaazon are genuine hold-up horses who will be forced closer than ideal. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a sustainable pace on quick ground with a bunched prominent pack behind — strongly favours those who can race handy and finish, giving the edge to settled prominent racers with a proven turn of foot on Good to Firm.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid is allowed to dictate unchallenged at a comfortable tempo through the first two furlongs and no prominent rival has the early pace to put her under pressure.
scenarios.body: Namiid rolls along at her own rhythm on Good to Firm ground where she has shown strong form, hitting the rising ground into the Curragh finish with enough left in reserve to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Fliers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Real Encounter, Final Melody, Sovereign Cry — push Namiid harder than expected and one uses the pace as a launching pad to overtake late.
scenarios.body: The pace stays honest enough to suit a finisher coming from just off the lead, and a well-positioned prominent type gets a clear run to reel in Namiid inside the final furlong on the quick surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong due to a bunched, competitive early stretch and the hold-up horses find a clear passage through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Focaccia or Daneh Of Dandy, sitting in behind the prominent scrummage, benefit from a wall of tiring horses in front and pick up ground late; however, with many hold-up types redistributed forward, a true sustained late run is hard to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group collectively goes too quick early and the entire field concertinas, creating a chaotic finish where a fresh-legged runner from the rear outfinishes everyone.
scenarios.body: The field compresses in the final 100 yards and a horse such as Tawaazon or Nebrook Star, racing from off the pace, benefits from tired rivals in front but this scenario requires multiple horses racing against their nature.

watchPoints.text: Namiid holds the race by the throat as sole pace-setter — if Jessica Maye (7lb claimer) settles her perfectly, watch for a front-running performance that is very hard to peg back on this Good to Firm surface.

Sovereign Cry won here 14 days ago over this exact course and trip and returns with Terry Casey's 7lb claim — a horse in-form at the track with weight allowance is a prime dangers in the prominent group.

The cluster of prominent types — Real Encounter, Final Melody, Happy Henry and Carrigans Grove — will create a scrimmage for positions in the first two furlongs; any runner drawn wide could lose lengths fighting for the rail and effectively race from a different position than planned.

Nebrook Star has not raced in 175 days — a three-year-old returning from near six months off into an 18-runner Good to Firm sprint is a significant fitness risk and could affect others if it checks sharply from the gates.

Multiple hold-up horses (Harry's Hill, Mary Shoelaces, Imperial Dream, Absoluteassignment, Tawaazon) are all jostling for the same rear-of-field positions — traffic and lack of a clear run in the final furlong is a real structural risk for all of them collectively.
